sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for the root layout
sections.what: Brings in the navigation stack, the status bar, the data loading library and the theme colors.
sections.why: Reason not stated beyond the file's role as the top layout.

sections.name: queryClient
sections.title: Shared data loading rules
sections.what: Creates the one shared data client. It retries failed requests twice, keeps results fresh for five minutes, and holds them in memory for ten minutes.
sections.why: Likely reason: fewer repeated server calls and faster screens. Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: Results can be up to five minutes old, so a change made elsewhere may not show until a refresh.

sections.name: RootLayout
sections.title: Top-level screen frame
sections.what: Wraps everything in the data provider and a light status bar. Then it lists the login group, the tabs group, and five full-screen pages: documents, family, analytics, settings and notifications. The five pages slide up from the bottom.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. The list decides which screens the app can open.
sections.watch_out: A route used elsewhere in the app but not listed here will not be found.

summary: The top-level layout that wraps the whole app. It sets up shared data loading and the status bar, and lists the main screens.
purpose: Acts as the outer frame. Every screen in the app sits inside it.
why: Reason not stated beyond the comments. The query provider lets all screens share cached server data.
how: Creates one shared query client with retry and caching rules. Wraps the app in that provider, shows a light status bar, and lists the stack of screens: the login group, the tabs group, and several full-screen pages opened from the bottom.
inputs: Server data requested by any screen through the shared client.
outputs: The app frame and screen transitions. This file saves nothing.
risks: Only some routes are registered here. Other links, such as privacy or help, have no entry in this file. Cached data stays fresh for five minutes, so changes may show late. Failed requests are retried twice, which delays error messages.
debug: If a screen will not open, check whether it is listed in the stack. If data looks old, check the freshness time. If errors show up slowly, check the retry count.
